_comment: Per-app style lines. Rendered as the first line of the user message: 'Style: <text>'. Trusted (comes from the app, not the screen). Keep each line short and never contradict the system prompt. 'default' is used when the category is unknown. Users may override a category's text in Settings; the override replaces 'text' verbatim.

messaging.label: Messengers
messaging.text: Casual chat message. Keep it natural and as short as the speaker made it; keep informal words and emoji names as spoken. A single short sentence may end without a period.

email.label: Email
email.text: Email. Use complete sentences and paragraphs; put a greeting and a sign-off on their own lines only if they were dictated.

notes.label: Notes and documents
notes.text: Notes or a document. Use paragraphs, and lists or headings only when the speaker clearly structured the content that way.

work_chat.label: Work chat (Slack, Teams, Mattermost)
work_chat.text: Work chat message. Clear and concise; keep technical terms, @mentions, file names and code identifiers exactly as on screen.

code.label: Code editors and terminals
code.text: Technical input. Keep identifiers, commands, paths and flags exactly as on screen; do not capitalize or add punctuation to commands; wrap nothing in quotes unless dictated.

search.label: Search and address bars
search.text: Search query. Short, no final period, no capitalization of ordinary words, keep it as a query.

social.label: Social posts and comments
social.text: Social media post or comment. Keep the speaker's voice and informal style; do not add hashtags or emoji that were not dictated.

default.label: Everything else
default.text: Neutral. Clean, correctly punctuated text in the speaker's own words.

address.label: Address fields (email, URL)
address.text: Address field. Output the literal address or identifier only: spoken 'at'/'собака' as @, 'dot'/'точка' as '.', no spaces, no capitalization, no final period.

field_overrides._comment: Applied after the app category, from the focused field's AccessibilityNodeInfo.getInputType() variation bits (android.text.InputType). Password variations never reach the LLM (see CONTEXT_AND_PROMPT.md, privacy).
